## Scope

This is the second CellCharterR tutorial. It covers the disk-backed import and
portable storage patterns needed for large H5AD spatial datasets. For a general
large H5AD, `cellcharter_import_h5ad()` creates an independent, resumable directory
without requiring Python, `anndataR`, `zellkonverter`, or R 4.5:

```{r general-large-import, eval=FALSE}
library(CellCharterR)

spe <- cellcharter_import_h5ad(
  h5ad_file = "large_spatial_dataset.h5ad",
  output_dir = "large_spatial_dataset_spe"
)

# The entire directory is portable; move the directory as one unit.
spe <- cellcharter_load_spe("large_spatial_dataset_spe")
spe
SpatialExperiment::spatialCoordsNames(spe)
SingleCellExperiment::reducedDimNames(spe)
SingleCellExperiment::colPairNames(spe)
names(S4Vectors::metadata(spe)$anndata_uns)
```

Large arrays stay on disk, while the returned SPE is independent of the source
H5AD because the directory owns its copied HDF5 payload. The complete AnnData
hierarchy remains in `arrays.h5`; requested `obs`, `var`, and `obsm` fields are
mapped to SPE structures, supported sparse `obsp` matrices become weighted
`colPairs`, and `uns` remains on disk with a locator in SPE metadata. Sparse
connectivity and distance values are preserved rather than recomputed. The remaining sections
document the stricter two-file CODEX conversion used by the mouse-spleen
reproduction.

This vignette documents the exact conversion used for the CellCharterR CODEX
reproduction. Its download and full conversion chunks deliberately have
`eval=FALSE`: package builds and checks must stay offline and must not download
the 600.4 MiB of H5AD data (151.9 MiB raw plus 448.5 MiB clustered).

The project uses a custom `read_codex_spe()` reader built from `rhdf5`,
`HDF5Array`, `DelayedArray`, and `SpatialExperiment`. It does **not** use
`zellkonverter` or `anndataR`. For general H5AD files, users should consider
those packages first because they support broader AnnData conventions. The
custom reader exists to enforce the exact identity and disk-backed layout of
these two versioned CODEX artifacts.

## Download the official files

Choose the destination yourself. The code writes partial files, verifies
SHA-256 checksums, and only then publishes the final names.

```{r download, eval=FALSE}
destination <- file.path("data-raw", "codex-mouse-spleen")
dir.create(destination, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

files <- data.frame(
  filename = c(
    "codex_mouse_spleen.h5ad",
    "codex_mouse_spleen_clustered.h5ad"
  ),
  url = c(
    "https://api.figshare.com/v2/file/download/38538101",
    "https://api.figshare.com/v2/file/download/46832722"
  ),
  sha256 = c(
    "b386cb72b20d483d3c84675bffcdd22cae1e4db6e4333271bc2c3bdf4ecef946",
    "a23434e23cbfb421b2f51593eb71fe5d642c545aca705e4607a4b2a081047bd6"
  ),
  md5 = c(
    "7d5ad7727ac214bcd61a55b2572ceb36",
    "b3d50ea1181b59b7b8fc0522633badb2"
  )
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(files))) {
  final <- file.path(destination, files$filename[[i]])
  partial <- paste0(final, ".partial")

  # Reuse an already complete download, but never trust its name alone.
  if (file.exists(final)) {
    valid_sha256 <- identical(
      digest::digest(file = final, algo = "sha256", serialize = FALSE),
      files$sha256[[i]]
    )
    valid_md5 <- identical(unname(tools::md5sum(final)), files$md5[[i]])
    if (valid_sha256 && valid_md5) next
    stop("Existing final file has the wrong checksum: ", final)
  }

  utils::download.file(files$url[[i]], partial, mode = "wb", method = "libcurl")
  observed_sha256 <- digest::digest(file = partial, algo = "sha256", serialize = FALSE)
  observed_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(partial))
  if (!identical(observed_sha256, files$sha256[[i]]) ||
      !identical(observed_md5, files$md5[[i]])) {
    stop("Checksum mismatch for ", files$filename[[i]])
  }
  if (!file.rename(partial, final)) stop("Could not publish ", final)
}
```

Equivalent shell downloads may use `curl -L` or `wget`, followed by `sha256sum`.
The R version above avoids assuming either shell program is installed.

## Convert to a disk-backed SpatialExperiment

```{r convert, eval=FALSE}
library(CellCharterR)

spe <- read_codex_spe(
  raw_h5ad = file.path(destination, "codex_mouse_spleen.h5ad"),
  clustered_h5ad = file.path(destination, "codex_mouse_spleen_clustered.h5ad"),
  representation_dataset = "obsm/X_trVAE",
  spatial_dataset = "obsm/spatial"
)

spe
SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(spe)
SingleCellExperiment::reducedDimNames(spe)
SpatialExperiment::spatialCoordsNames(spe)
```

The protein assay and trVAE representation remain HDF5-backed. The canonical
two-column `spatialCoords()` matrix is realized in memory (about 10.8 MiB for
707,474 segmented cells), as required by `SpatialExperiment`; the large assay and
representation are not materialized. The reader validates global or
sample-scoped cell identities and will not accept positional coincidence as
proof of alignment.

The package includes a miniature two-file fixture with the same storage
contract, so the actual custom conversion can be demonstrated offline:

```{r tiny-conversion}
library(CellCharterR)

tiny_raw <- system.file(
  "extdata", "codex_mouse_spleen_tiny_raw.h5ad",
  package = "CellCharterR", mustWork = TRUE
)
tiny_clustered <- system.file(
  "extdata", "codex_mouse_spleen_tiny_clustered.h5ad",
  package = "CellCharterR", mustWork = TRUE
)
tiny_from_h5ad <- read_codex_spe(tiny_raw, tiny_clustered)
tiny_from_h5ad
SingleCellExperiment::reducedDimNames(tiny_from_h5ad)
head(SpatialExperiment::spatialCoords(tiny_from_h5ad))
```

This disk-backed object depends on the H5AD files staying at their recorded
locations. It is appropriate for scalable computation, but it is not the
portable distribution artifact.

## Create a movable SpatialExperiment

To move one object elsewhere and forget the H5AD files, explicitly realize the
arrays as ordinary matrices and build a new object. This needs enough RAM for
all selected fields.

```{r portable, eval=FALSE}
portable <- SpatialExperiment::SpatialExperiment(
  assays = list(
    protein = as.matrix(SummarizedExperiment::assay(spe, "protein"))
  ),
  rowData = SummarizedExperiment::rowData(spe),
  colData = SummarizedExperiment::colData(spe),
  reducedDims = S4Vectors::SimpleList(
    X_trVAE = as.matrix(SingleCellExperiment::reducedDim(spe, "X_trVAE"))
  ),
  spatialCoords = as.matrix(SpatialExperiment::spatialCoords(spe)),
  sample_id = as.character(SummarizedExperiment::colData(spe)$sample),
  metadata = S4Vectors::metadata(spe)
)

saveRDS(portable, "CellCharterR_mouse_spleen_spe.rds")
```

The validated canonical portable artifact is 286.0 MiB on disk and occupies
approximately 693.7 MiB after loading in R. Its SHA-256 is
`d9adda271ad26aca5887a2d4f38feea8bb3a1503b561e34ee9f13df129371219`.
It is deliberately not bundled inside the software package; the project must
publish it as a separate data product before assigning a durable download URL.
The packaged teaching `SpatialExperiment` retains the same deterministic 1,000
cell identities and stores coordinates canonically in `spatialCoords()`.

The repository's
`inst/scripts/make-codex-portable-and-tiny.R` additionally attaches the already
checkpointed aggregate representation, K=4 primary labels, K=11 sensitivity
labels, checksums, and a deterministic 1,000-segmented-cell subset. It does not recompute
the full analysis.

## Provenance and licenses

The original CODEX dataset is CC BY 4.0 and is described by
doi:10.17632/zjnpwh8m5b.1. The clustered H5AD and AutoK resources are CC BY 4.0
under doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.25040192.v2. Cite the original CODEX publication
